cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Lost in the Process
cards.instruction: Hide your role in the problem by distributing blame across steps, policies, and unnamed procedures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parcel was lost between dispatch and transport. Let me complete the incident report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left it on the bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please keep the stages separate. Dispatch released it; transport failed to confirm receipt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both departments are you. Call the bus company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the route number. I'll report a handover failure. Under responsibility, put 'dispatch and receipt control'; don't collapse two stages into one name.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects responsibility into separate stages and A5 supervises report categories, using professional classification to diffuse A's blame.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 names the bus mistake; A3 divides it into departments; B4 identifies their single operator, causing A5 a multi-stage responsibility entry.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 want the lost parcel recovered and reject evasive classification, a credible practical concern.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts calling the company while preventing B4 from collapsing the stages into A's name.

specificity.evidence: A1 parcel report and B2 bus explain the loss without an invented workplace.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 route request and responsibility entry serve the same call/report, though the final turn is relatively full.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 exposes A3 departments as A and requests the recovery call.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 uses B4 call to dictate a distributed responsibility entry.
